title: Light Up The House
tagline: Third-person sci-fi repair adventure: fix three broken systems before the countdown hits zero.
type: Team of 3 · Unreal Engine 5 · NED GameCon'26
contributions: Led development as game developer and project manager for a 3-person team, coordinating scope and delivery in UE5.

Built the tool and appliance interaction loop: pickup (press I) and fix (press E) logic, tied to a BPI_Interaction Blueprint Interface so every interactable actor (tools, appliances) shares a common contract. The interface uses enum-driven logic and is reusable across actors.

Implemented the UI/UX system across the Widget Blueprint stack: splash screen, main menu (hover animations, settings overlay with volume slider, quit logic), pause menu, and the proximity-based "Info Card" system that detects when the player nears a broken appliance and shows the correct tool using On Actor Begin/End Overlap.
Handled win/loss state management through the Level Manager.
description: Light Up The House is a third-person sci-fi exploration-adventure built in Unreal Engine 5. You play Mr. Robo, a robotic operative aboard a space shuttle that has lost total power. The objective: find the right tool for each of three broken systems, repair them before a countdown timer hits zero, and light the house back up.
collaborators: M. Faisal Hameed and M. Huzaifa

title: The Floor Is A Liar
tagline: A 3D browser game where the rules might be lying to you.
contributions: Designed the rule mechanic, tile effects, level progression and scoring system.
Built the Three.js scene in React Three Fiber, with a follow camera, lighting, an animated character and portal, and raycast-based hover and click-to-move.
Fixed mobile usability by adjusting the camera for portrait view.
Designed the Supabase/PostgreSQL schema with Row Level Security, validated save functions and a privacy-safe leaderboard.
Wrote 69 automated tests across 12 suites, including real raycasting and level-solvability tests.
Deployed with Git and Vercel CI/CD and documented the project.
description: FloorIsALiar is a disco-themed 3D puzzle-arcade game. Players cross a floating dance floor of colored tiles to reach an exit portal. Each round, a loudspeaker announces a rule about one tile color, such as "Orange tiles are slippery!", and the rule can be true or a lie. Players must decide whether to trust it, and whether to take the short risky route or the long safe one. It ships with accounts, saved runs, a stats dashboard and a global leaderboard.

title: VR Escape Room
tagline: Collect 4 keys against the clock to escape the mansion, in VR.
contributions: Investigated and implemented VR teleportation and pickup interactions, testing multiple interaction models for usability.
Built visual feedback cues (glow and float effects) to test how affordance guides player behavior.
Iteratively tuned puzzle pacing through playtesting, adjusting key placement and unlock logic based on real player feedback.

description: A VR escape room built to explore how physical interaction models and visual feedback affect player behavior in 3D space. Goal: the player needs to collect 4 keys under a time constraint in order to escape the mansion, but on each collection gets teleported to a new area. The screen starts flashing red when the player starts to run out of time, adding difficulty and visual distress.

title: Oakridge Hollow
tagline: A Minecraft-inspired 3D voxel sandbox that runs 100% in the browser.
contributions: Designed and built the 3D voxel engine, procedural texture and audio generators, dual camera controls, NPC behavior and a responsive HUD from scratch.
Procedural World & Foraging: generated seeded rolling terrain, a pond, a lantern-lit cottage, and oak trees that drop collectible, edible apples when harvested.
Mining, Building & Inventory Loop: built raycast block breaking and placing with particle bursts, spinning 3D pickups, and an 8-slot live resource hotbar.
Roaming Villagers & Animals: modeled and animated villagers (with speech bubbles) and farm animals (sheep, pigs, chickens) that navigate terrain and avoid water.
Dual Camera & Trackpad-Friendly UX: added a quick Break/Place mode switcher (Q), Orbit View, First-Person Walk/Fly mode (WASD), and a Settings modal.
Automated Day / Dusk / Night Cycle: built smooth lighting, sky and shadow transitions that cycle automatically every 90 seconds or manually via Settings.
Rendering: stores voxels in a spatial Map ("x,y,z" to blockType) with neighbor-based face culling, and draws deterministic 16x16 pixel-art canvas bitmaps mapped with THREE.NearestFilter.
Procedural Audio (Web Audio API): synthesizes block crunches, footsteps, animal and villager calls, and ambient chimes in real time using noise buffers, bandpass filters and oscillators.
description: Oakridge Hollow is a browser-based, Minecraft-inspired 3D voxel sandbox built with Three.js and the Web Audio API for a Web 3D Programming course. It runs 100% client-side with zero external assets. All pixel-art textures, terrain, animated villagers and animals, day-dusk-night lighting and sound effects are generated procedurally in code.

title: Shadows of the Slums
tagline: A maze-escape thriller: witness a gang murder, then survive.
contributions: Owned one full scene independently, building it end to end.
Environment: designed the maze sequence and pacing for that section of the escape.
Systems: programmed core gameplay in C#, including character movement, animation state control and scene-switching logic.

Narrative: designed and validated the trust-based NPC dialogue system central to the story. Since the worker's survival depends on which NPCs choose to help him, I mapped out how trust would be earned or lost.
description: Shadows of the Slums is a maze-escape thriller built in Unity3D by a 3-person team. The story follows a regular worker who witnesses a gang murder and gets seen by the killer. Now marked, he has to survive, evade the mafia, and find a way to expose them, relying on NPCs he can (or cannot) trust to help him along the way. Each of the three of us owned one full scene end to end: environment, NPC dialogue and animation.

title: AR Piano
tagline: An air piano: play notes by pressing keys in mid-air, tracked by webcam.
contributions: Built the full pipeline solo: hand and finger landmark tracking using MediaPipe, and real-time video processing with OpenCV.
Wrote the logic that maps tracked finger positions to on-screen key zones and triggers the corresponding note.
Solved the gesture-to-input problem: detecting a "press" reliably (a finger crossing a key's threshold) without false triggers from natural hand movement.
description: An AR air piano built in Python using OpenCV and MediaPipe. A webcam tracks your hand in real time, maps finger positions to piano keys rendered on screen, and plays notes when you "press" a key in mid-air, with no physical keyboard involved.

title: Six of Crows Trailer
tagline: A TV-series opening sequence for Six of Crows, made with motion graphics.
contributions: Parallax compositing: layered sky, tree silhouette and birds at different depths with a simulated camera push for scene depth.
Luma matte transition: dissolved black into the title card using a smoke/ink matte.
Kinetic typography: animated the title build ("SI" to "SIX OF CROWS") with After Effects text range selectors.
Null-parented rig: built a reusable card fan using a fixed rotational offset per layer, parented to a null.
3D layer animation: flipped each character card into frame using 3D rotation.
Blend mode compositing: layered a smoke texture in Screen mode behind the cards for depth without hard edges.
Shape wipe transition: used a bird silhouette as a wipe between the title and card sequence.
description: For my final project in the post-production course at the Centre of Excellence for Gaming and Animation (CEGA), I adapted my favourite book, Six of Crows, into a TV-series opening sequence using motion graphics.
